usage_md:
# ProxyPilot Auth — integration notes

Local password + LDAPS authentication, JWT access tokens with rotating hashed
refresh tokens, DB-driven RBAC with per-role permission overrides, an
encrypted-at-rest LDAPS connection settings service, and a race-safe first-admin
(superadmin) bootstrap. Extracted from the ADP project and decoupled so the host
injects its Drizzle client + config once at boot.

The runner copies these files into the project. **No application code is modified
for you** — do the wiring in steps 2–6 below.

## 1. Dependencies

Runtime (the module imports these):

```
npm install cookie ldapts zod
```

Peers the host app already provides (install if missing):

```
npm install drizzle-orm express pg
```

Dev (only if you run the shipped tests):

```
npm install -D vitest @types/express @types/node @types/pg
```

There is no automatic dependency install on import — run the lines above.

## 2. Mount / wiring example

All module code lands under `src/auth/`. Import from `./auth/index.js` (this is an
ESM/NodeNext codebase — keep the `.js` extension on relative imports).

```ts
// src/server.ts (or wherever you build the app)
import express from 'express';
import { drizzle } from 'drizzle-orm/node-postgres';
import pg from 'pg';
import {
  initAuth, loadAuthConfigFromEnv, authSchema,
  withAuth, bootstrapGate, authRoutes, adminAuthRoutes, wireLdapsFromConfig,
} from './auth/index.js';
import * as appSchema from './db/schema.js';

// (a) Build ONE Drizzle client that also knows the auth tables.
const pool = new pg.Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL });
const db = drizzle(pool, { schema: { ...appSchema, ...authSchema } });

// (b) Inject db + config once, BEFORE mounting routers or serving a request.
initAuth({
  db,
  config: loadAuthConfigFromEnv(),   // or resolveAuthConfig({ ...yourConfig })
  hooks: {
    // Optional. Fires once, right after the first superadmin is created.
    // Replaces the ADP-specific initProfileFromBootstrap. Omit for a no-op.
    async onSuperadminCreated({ tenantId, email, userId }) {
      // e.g. seed a profile row from `email`
    },
  },
});

// (c) Wire the live LDAPS transport (no-op unless LDAPS_TRANSPORT=ldapts).
await wireLdapsFromConfig({ probe: true });

// (d) Mount middleware + routers.
const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
app.use(withAuth);                 // attaches req.auth (tenant + role) to every request
app.use(bootstrapGate());          // REQUIRED — forces the first-admin bootstrap (see §5)
app.use('/api', authRoutes);       // /api/auth/bootstrap/*, /login, /refresh, /logout, /setup/*
app.use('/api', adminAuthRoutes);  // /api/admin/permissions*, /admin/users*, /admin/ldaps*

// (e) Serve the sign-in page + its scripts from public/.
app.get('/login', (_req, res) =>
  res.sendFile('login.html', { root: 'public' }));
app.use(express.static('public', { index: false }));
```

Guard your own routes with the exported middleware:

```ts
import { requireRole, requirePermission } from './auth/index.js';
app.post('/api/reports/sync', requireRole('manager'), handler);      // manager or admin
app.get('/api/settings',      requirePermission('admin.settings'), handler);
```

`initAuth()` must run before any auth code executes — using the module before it
throws a clear "not initialized" error rather than failing obscurely.

## 3. Configuration (env vars / config keys)

Pass a resolved `AuthConfig` to `initAuth`. `loadAuthConfigFromEnv()` reads these;
all are optional with dev-safe defaults — **override the two secrets in
production**.

| Key | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTH_JWT_SECRET` | `dev-insecure-…` | **SECRET.** HS256 key that signs access tokens. |
| `AUTH_MASTER_SECRET` | `dev-insecure-…` | **SECRET.** Derives the AES-256-GCM key encrypting the stored LDAPS bind password + CA. |
| `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` | `900` (15 min) | Access-token lifetime. |
| `REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` | `604800` (7 d) | Refresh-token lifetime. |
| `REFRESH_GRACE_SECONDS` | `30` | Concurrent-refresh grace window. |
| `SESSION_IDLE_SECONDS` | `604800` | Idle timeout for a refresh token. |
| `LDAPS_TRANSPORT` | `ldapts` | `ldapts` \| `fake` \| `none`. `wireLdapsFromConfig` wires the real socket client only for `ldapts`. |
| `TRUST_PROXY_AUTH` | `false` | Trust `x-user-role`/`x-tenant-id` headers — see caveats. |
| `NODE_ENV` | `development` | `production` makes the session cookies `Secure`. |

The Postgres connection is **not** part of this config — you inject the Drizzle
`db`. The CLI and migration read `DATABASE_URL` from the environment directly.

## 4. Layout notes

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `src/auth/*.ts` | The module. Entry point is `src/auth/index.js` (barrel). `context.ts` holds the injected db/config; `config.ts` defines `AuthConfig`. |
| `src/auth/types/cookie.d.ts` | Ambient types for `cookie`. Your `tsconfig` must include `src/auth/**` so it's picked up. |
| `src/auth/test-support/` | Test helper that loads the shipped browser module. |
| `src/auth/*.test.ts` | Vitest unit suite — 39 tests, no DB or network needed. Runs under the project's Vitest (`npx vitest run`). Delete these files if the project doesn't run tests. |
| `public/login.html`, `login.js`, `rbac-shared.js` | Sign-in page + scripts. Serve `public/` statically and `login.html` at `/login`. |
| `migrations/0001_auth.sql` | Creates `roles`, `users`, `refresh_tokens`, `role_permission_overrides`, `auth_connections`, `auth_audit_log` and seeds the `admin`/`manager`/`viewer` roles. Renumber to slot after your existing migrations. |
| `scripts/bootstrap-superadmin.mjs` | CLI to seed/update the pending superadmin (reads `DATABASE_URL`). |

**Kept-in-sync invariant:** `public/rbac-shared.js` mirrors the server's canonical
role slugs from `src/auth/roles.ts`; `src/auth/rbac-shared-consistency.test.ts`
fails if they drift. The `CONNECTION_EDIT_IDS` / `applyConnectionRbac` helper in
`rbac-shared.js` still carries ADP-specific DOM IDs (`adp-client-id`, `cert-pem`,
…) — those are an **example** for a settings screen; replace them with your own
screen's IDs. The role-slug half is the part that must stay in sync.

Declare your app's permissions in `src/auth/permissions.ts`. What ships is only
what this component's own admin screens check (`admin.dashboard`,
`admin.settings`, `admin.connections`, `admin.users`) — add a key for every
permissioned surface you build, with the roles that should hold it by default.
An undeclared key never reaches Admin → Permissions and `PUT /admin/permissions`
rejects it (`UNKNOWN_PERMISSION`), so a manager or viewer can never be granted
it; an admin holds it regardless, because `defaultAllows` grants admin anything
the map has not heard of. Per-role overrides live in the
`role_permission_overrides` table and always win over the map.

## 5. Bootstrap the first admin (FORCED — do not re-implement)

`bootstrapGate()` (mounted in step (d) — REQUIRED) makes the first-run flow
impossible to miss: while ZERO users exist, every browser navigation is
redirected to the sign-in page — which shows the create-administrator form —
and every non-bootstrap API call returns `503 BOOTSTRAP_REQUIRED`. The moment
the first superadmin is created the gate settles into a cached no-op.

Rules for the integrating build:

- **Mount `bootstrapGate()` exactly as shown in step (d).** Skipping it, or
  building your own first-run/landing logic instead, is a re-implementation of
  capability this component already provides.
- **If you build a custom sign-in page**, it MUST call
  `GET /api/auth/bootstrap/status` on load and, while `canCreateSuperadmin` is
  true, show ONLY the create-administrator form (POST
  `/api/auth/bootstrap/superadmin`, password >= 12 chars) — exactly as the
  shipped `public/login.js` does. Copy its boot sequence; do not invent a
  parallel one. Role pickers, self-signup tabs, and normal login render only
  AFTER the first administrator exists.
- Accounts on the reserved fixture domain `@fixture.invalid` (created by the
  build platform's automated UI checks) never count toward first-time state:
  `usersExist` and both first-admin guards exclude them, so test fixtures can
  exist without consuming the operator's first-admin bootstrap.
- Do not seed an admin user in a migration to "skip" the flow — the race-safe
  bootstrap (or the CLI below) is the only supported path.

Either let the sign-in page create it (the gate guarantees the form is what a
first visitor sees), or seed a pending admin from the CLI:

```
DATABASE_URL=postgres://… node scripts/bootstrap-superadmin.mjs admin@corp.com [tenantId]
```

It refuses to touch an already-active admin and uses the same race-safe
`NOT EXISTS` guard as the HTTP bootstrap, so the two can't both create a first
admin. The account can't log in until first-time password setup completes via
`POST /api/auth/setup/password`.

## One-time sign-in links (account setup / password reset)

No temporary passwords: an admin issues a link (`POST /api/admin/users/:id/login-link`,
also the Users page's "Sign-in link" button); the user opens it
(`/login#link=<token>`), chooses a password, and is signed in.

- **Preview-safe by design.** `GET /api/auth/link/status` never mutates —
  email/SMS scanners that prefetch the URL cannot spend it. The link is
  consumed ONLY when the password is set (`POST /api/auth/link/complete`),
  which also voids every other open link for that user.
- Raw token exists only in the issued URL; the table stores its sha256.
  7-day expiry. Deactivated users' links stop validating immediately.
- **Forgot password:** issue a new link for the user — their old password
  keeps working until the link is used (a reset request can never lock the
  account). To automate email/SMS delivery, call `issueLoginLink()` from your
  own handler and send `origin + path` through your `sendEmail`/SMS hook.
- Migration `migrations/0003_login_links.sql` creates the table (renumber to
  slot after your existing migrations, as usual).

## 6. Security caveats

- **`TRUST_PROXY_AUTH` is default-off on purpose.** A client-supplied `x-user-role`
  header grants nothing unless you set this true — and you should set it true ONLY
  when the app sits behind ProxyPilot's edge proxy, which strips those headers from
  every inbound client request before injecting verified ones. Leaving it off is
  what makes a spoofed `x-user-role: admin` (no credential) get rejected on the
  direct path. Turning it on without that header-stripping proxy is a full auth
  bypass.
- **Rotate the secrets.** `AUTH_JWT_SECRET` and `AUTH_MASTER_SECRET` ship with
  insecure dev defaults; inject real values from your secrets manager in
  production. `AUTH_MASTER_SECRET` protects the stored LDAPS bind password —
  rotating it makes existing encrypted connections undecryptable (re-enter them).
- **Cookies are `Secure` only when `NODE_ENV=production`.** Serve over HTTPS in
  production so the httpOnly access/refresh cookies aren't sent in cleartext.
- **No LDAPS auto-provisioning.** An LDAPS-authenticated user with no local account
  is rejected — users must be invited/created first. This is intentional; don't
  "fix" it by creating accounts on the fly.
- Secrets, tokens, and the LDAPS private key are never logged; keep it that way if
  you extend the audit metadata.


## External (self-signup) accounts — outside individuals

LDAPS covers **employees**; some apps also serve **outside individuals** — the
canonical example is a credentialing portal where providers sign up with their
own email to submit licenses. External accounts are:

- **Off by default.** An admin flips `auth_settings.external_signup`
  (`PUT /api/admin/external { "enabled": true }`, audited) or the settings UI
  built on it. `GET /api/auth/signup/status` tells the login page whether to
  show a "Create account" tab at all.
- **Email + password signup** (`POST /api/auth/signup`), with **email
  verification** when a `sendEmail` hook is wired: the account stays inactive
  (login refused) until the emailed link/code is used
  (`POST /api/auth/signup/verify`, resend via `/signup/resend`, 1/min).
  With no email sender wired the account activates immediately (dev-friendly).
  Existing-address signups return the same response as new ones — no account
  enumeration.
- **Least privileged.** They hold the `external` role — below `viewer` in the
  ranking, so every existing `requireRole('viewer')` guard already excludes
  them, and they appear in no `DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS` entry.

### The visibility rule (self-only vs see-everything)

```ts
import { ownerScopeUserId, canAccessOwnedResource, requireInternal } from './auth/index.js';

// Lists: external → only their rows; internal (admin/manager/viewer) → all rows.
const scope = ownerScopeUserId(getAuth(req));           // number | null
const rows = scope === null
  ? await db.select().from(licenses)
  : await db.select().from(licenses).where(eq(licenses.ownerUserId, scope));

// Single-row reads/writes:
if (!canAccessOwnedResource(getAuth(req), row.ownerUserId)) return res.status(404).end();

// Employee-only surfaces (staff lists, admin screens):
app.use('/api/staff', requireInternal, staffRoutes);
```

Give every externally-owned table an `owner_user_id` column and apply
`ownerScopeUserId` on **every** list/read — the external user sees only their
own account; internal employees see all submitting accounts and can pull any
documentation.

### Wiring

```ts
import externalAuthRoutes, { adminExternalRoutes } from './auth/external-routes.js';

initAuth({
  db, config,
  hooks: {
    sendEmail: (m) => sendEmail(m),                        // @proxypilot/email
    verificationUrl: (t) => `${APP_BASE_URL}/verify-email?token=${t}`,
  },
});
app.use('/api/auth', authRoutes);
app.use('/api/auth', externalAuthRoutes);                  // public signup endpoints
app.use('/api/admin/external', requirePermission('admin.users'), adminExternalRoutes);
```

Run `migrations/0002_auth_external.sql` (seeds the `external` role, adds
`users.account_type` / `email_verified_at`, `auth_settings`,
`email_verifications`). External users sign in through the normal
`POST /api/auth/login` — LDAPS is never consulted for them (`provider:
'builtin'`), and unverified accounts are refused as inactive.

-- 0005_auth — authentication + authorization module.
-- Per administrator-approved deviation from constitution §4, this project uses
-- JWT access tokens + hashed refresh tokens in the DB (local password auth with
-- an optional LDAPS fallback). Roles follow the CONFIRMED rules.md set only:
-- admin, manager, viewer (rule-q37/q46). No 'staff'/'payroll' roles exist.

-- DB-driven role system (text keys, not enum-locked).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS roles (
  key          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  label        TEXT NOT NULL,
  is_system    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  is_editable  BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  is_deletable BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Seed the three confirmed roles (rule-q24/q37). admin is system + locked;
-- manager/viewer are system + non-deletable but relabelable.
INSERT INTO roles (key, label, is_system, is_editable, is_deletable) VALUES
  ('admin',   'Admin',   true, false, false),
  ('manager', 'Manager', true, true,  false),
  ('viewer',  'Viewer',  true, true,  false)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING;

-- Application users. Email is unique case-insensitively (stored lower-cased).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  id                       SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id                TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default',
  email                    TEXT NOT NULL,
  password_hash            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  password_setup_required  BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  role                     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(key) ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  is_active                BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  provider                 TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'builtin', -- builtin | ldaps
  totp_secret              TEXT,
  totp_enabled             BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  last_login_at            TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at               TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
-- Case-insensitive uniqueness on email.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS users_email_unique ON users (lower(email));
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS users_role_idx ON users (role);

-- Hashed refresh tokens (only the hash is ever persisted). Rotation revokes the
-- prior token; a short grace window handles concurrent-refresh races.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS refresh_tokens (
  id          SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  token_hash  TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  expires_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  revoked_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS refresh_tokens_user_idx ON refresh_tokens (user_id);

-- Per-role/permission override rows. Effective permission = default map, then
-- override wins when a row exists.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS role_permission_overrides (
  role        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(key) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE,
  permission  TEXT NOT NULL,
  allowed     BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (role, permission)
);

-- Directory / integration connections, including LDAPS. Secrets are encrypted at
-- rest (ciphertext + nonce, AES-256-GCM); the plaintext JSON is never stored.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_connections (
  id                 SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default',
  provider           TEXT NOT NULL,              -- ldaps | ...
  label              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  status             TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unconfigured', -- unconfigured|ok|broken
  secret_ciphertext  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  secret_nonce       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  last_tested_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS auth_connections_provider_idx ON auth_connections (tenant_id, provider);

-- Audit evidence for auth/authz events (constitution §5: PII-aware, no secrets).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_audit_log (
  id             SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default',
  actor_user_id  INTEGER REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  action         TEXT NOT NULL,
  resource_type  TEXT,
  resource_id    TEXT,
  metadata       JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  ip             TEXT,
  user_agent     TEXT,
  created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS auth_audit_action_idx ON auth_audit_log (action);

-- 0002_auth_external — external (self-signup) accounts for the auth module.
--
-- The directory (LDAPS) covers EMPLOYEES; some apps also serve OUTSIDE
-- individuals — e.g. a credentialing portal where providers sign up with their
-- own email to submit licenses. External accounts:
--   * sign up themselves with email + password (feature is OFF by default —
--     an admin turns it on: auth_settings.external_signup);
--   * verify their email when an email sender is wired (unverified accounts
--     stay inactive and cannot log in);
--   * hold the least-privileged 'external' role: they see ONLY their own
--     account/data (ownerScopeUserId), while internal roles see everything.

-- The 'external' role — system, below viewer in the privilege ranking.
INSERT INTO roles (key, label, is_system, is_editable, is_deletable) VALUES
  ('external', 'External', true, true, false)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING;

-- internal (employees / operator-created) vs external (self-signed-up).
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS account_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'internal';
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email_verified_at TIMESTAMPTZ;

-- Module settings (small, admin-toggled). external_signup: {"enabled": bool}.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_settings (
  key        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  value      JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
INSERT INTO auth_settings (key, value) VALUES ('external_signup', '{"enabled": false}'::jsonb)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING;

-- One-shot email-verification tokens (random secret; only its SHA-256 hash is
-- stored — same posture as refresh tokens).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS email_verifications (
  id          SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  token_hash  TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  expires_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  used_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS email_verifications_user_idx ON email_verifications (user_id, created_at DESC);

-- One-time sign-in links (admin-issued account setup / password reset).
-- The RAW token lives only in the issued URL; this table stores its sha256.
-- Preview-safe by design: GET /api/auth/link/status never mutates — a link is
-- consumed ONLY when the password is actually set (completed_at stamped).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS login_links (
  id           SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  token_hash   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  created_by   INTEGER REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  expires_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_login_links_user ON login_links (user_id);
